queue.title: Your automated checks have not actually run since 22 July. Two breakages stacked and the second hid the first, so the whole test suite has been skipped in CI for 46 days -- including five checks that exist purely to shout when test data is missing. Local landing checks were unaffected. Fixing the obvious half returns it to the OLDER failure, not to green; the order is written down.

A reset can strand your in-game save, or in one case write an older save over a newer one. The old window flushes before resetting and says why; the new one does not. The test meant to catch this reads the emulator's memory and never the file, so it passes while blind. The only finding in the sweep that destroys your data.

About 560 real Z80 instructions crash the emulator outright rather than refusing, with nothing to catch it -- so one byte in a game's sound code kills the window or the server. Common in hand-written sound drivers, and a commercial game has already hit this class once.

The Z80 reset line only stops the clock; it resets nothing. A sound driver halted at the wrong moment stays halted forever and never restarts. Measured with controls. The rule was written into our own notes in July with 'pin it, do not let it drift' and never implemented.

Two video writes in one instruction charge the first one's delay twice -- 40 percent over-billed on the most common way games write video memory. The read path next door does it correctly. Every existing test stops one write short of triggering it.

The drift check I landed this morning covers none of the eleven symbols the Effects panel depends on -- measured, zero of 25 rows. Cheap, needs no decision from you, and it is the half of the frozen-fixture question worth doing on its own.

The rest of the lens sweep: 8 critical, 33 high, ~77 smaller, all in docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-06-oracle-lens-sweep.md with the derivation for each. Nothing is fixed -- the reviewers were read-only on purpose so the report stays honest. Most of these have their fix already written elsewhere in the tree; they are gaps in coverage, not in knowledge.

Landed as an Effects tab: pick a scene or raster effect from a list and the game switches, instead of holding START and a button. Nudging numbers is visible but disabled until the engine team adds one small piece. Turning bands off will refuse on your current window until you relaunch, because your loaded symbols predate the thing it points at. Nothing has been tried against a running game yet -- that happens when you relaunch, and it closes the pacing readout at the same time.

queue.title: Your lag report. The plane viewer only redraws when its picture changes -- but on the waterline and floor-fan rows the picture changes every frame by design, so it redraws the whole plane every frame and the saving never applies. Up to half a million pixel lookups per frame. Not confirmed as YOUR lag yet; the tab test confirms or clears it.
